answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency: each identity commits a predicted transaction profile per epoch; the next epoch's profile is checked against the prior one via a similarity score. Identities whose behaviour drifts beyond an ivory tolerance band are flagged and throttled. To bridge epochs undetected, an attacker must run fresh identities for several epochs before each attack, multiplying operational cost and delay per sybil. Persistent deviation below the horizon threshold forces retirement and restart.
